title: Deref Interface
concept: The Deref interface lets you use `*` on custom types — making wrappers and smart pointers behave like references to the inner type.
why: Without Deref, every wrapper type would require manual method forwarding. Deref makes wrappers transparent — you call inner methods directly.
tips: Only implement Deref when your type IS-A inner type semantically — not just for convenience
Deref coercion happens automatically for function arguments — &Wrapper → &Inner
Use Deref for newtype wrappers that should be transparent — callers see the inner API
Don't implement Deref if it would expose internal invariants to mutation
common_mistakes: Overusing Deref — every wrapper shouldn't Deref, only semantically meaningful ones
Implementing Deref on a type that breaks the inner type's invariants through mutation
Using Deref for 'has-a' relationships — use regular method access instead
